content.text:
I want to discuss and possibly work on: safely prevent forged Entire-Checkpoint trailers without breaking squash-merge resume

Context:
- Repository: entireio/cli. The target worktree is already on branch `fix-checkpoint-trailer-block`.
- This came from the explicit follow-up in https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2168: `FormatCheckpoint` accepts legitimate multi-line commit messages, and the checkpoint parsers currently search the whole message. A line-start `Entire-Checkpoint:` in user-controlled body text can therefore be interpreted as metadata.
- The worktree currently contains an uncommitted experiment: `ParseCheckpoint` and `ParseAllCheckpoints` feed only `finalTrailerBlock(commitMessage)` to their regexes, plus direct regression tests. The production logic is only two changed expressions.
- Focused trailer-package tests pass, but the experiment is not shippable as written. Existing CLI tests and the Vogon canary prove that GitHub squash messages and native `git merge --squash` messages legitimately preserve original checkpoint trailers in separate commit-body paragraphs. Final-block-only parsing causes `entire resume` to see only one checkpoint, breaking the supported “resume latest checkpoint from squash merge” behavior.
- Do not weaken or rewrite the real-format squash tests merely to make the strict parser pass. The relevant canary is `TestResumeSquashMergeMultipleCheckpoints`; relevant unit tests include `TestFindCheckpointInHistory_MultipleCheckpoints`, `TestFindBranchCheckpoint_SquashMergeMultipleCheckpoints`, and `TestResumeFromCurrentBranch_MultipleCheckpointsSaysLatest`.
- A Beads task, `en-wqo`, tracks this work and remains open.

Before doing any implementation:
- Find the `entireio/cli` repository and switch to the existing `fix-checkpoint-trailer-block` worktree/branch.
- Read the local AGENTS.md and repository instructions.
- Inspect the current uncommitted diff, the checkpoint trailer parsers, every production caller of `ParseCheckpoint` and `ParseAllCheckpoints`, the squash-resume tests, recent history, and the live state of PR #2168.
- Perform an extensive independent review of the threat model and existing behavior. Decide whether this task is still real, whether final-block-only parsing is a good idea, and whether a smaller or safer boundary exists.
- Explicitly call out whether the current experiment should be discarded, narrowed, or evolved. Look for stale assumptions and avoid treating a syntactically two-line patch as a complete fix merely because it is small.

Task:
- If the review supports implementation, design and implement a fix that prevents untrusted checkpoint-shaped commit-body text from being accepted in unsafe contexts while preserving legitimate multi-checkpoint discovery and “latest checkpoint” resume for real GitHub and git-CLI squash formats.
- Consider whether singular trusted-trailer parsing and multi-checkpoint historical discovery need separate APIs or validation rules, and whether discovered checkpoint IDs can be verified against repository checkpoint storage before they affect behavior. Treat these as starting hypotheses, not prescribed architecture.
- Keep changes scoped to this security/correctness boundary. Do not modify unrelated trailer types or remove squash-resume functionality without an explicit product decision.
- Preserve existing user changes and do not use destructive git commands.

Validation:
- Add a focused regression proving the actual forged-body failure is rejected at the correct trust boundary.
- Keep the existing real-format squash unit tests and `TestResumeSquashMergeMultipleCheckpoints` passing without changing them into synthetic final-block-only fixtures.
- Run focused unit tests first, then the repository-required `mise run check`. The first historical full-gate attempt also encountered unrelated load-sensitive failures, but a rerun cleared them; distinguish genuine regressions from baseline flakes with focused reproduction.
- Do not run paid real-agent E2E tests. The Vogon canary included by `mise run check` is expected and safe.

Output:
- Start with review findings and a recommendation, including the security-versus-compatibility tradeoff.
- Then provide the proposed plan or patch summary.
- If you edit code, keep the change scoped, report exact tests and results, and close `en-wqo` only when the objective is genuinely complete.
- Do not push, merge, close GitHub issues/PRs, label, or post public comments unless explicitly told.

I’m using the `session-start` skill to load the Beads task and repository state, then `using-entire` to recover historical intent before judging the current experiment. I’ll begin with a read-only review; I’ll only evolve the patch if the evidence supports a safe compatibility-preserving boundary.

content.text:
Review complete: the task is real, but the current final-block-only experiment is too broad. It closes the mutation-path forgery while also erasing the deliberately supported squash-history semantics.

My recommendation is to evolve it into two explicit trust levels:

- Keep whole-message parsing for historical checkpoint discovery, where GitHub and native squash commits legitimately embed several trailers as body paragraphs.
- Add strict final-trailer-block parsing for decisions that can create, append to, or reuse checkpoint storage—especially commit hooks and attach.
- Treat storage lookup as validation that an ID exists, not authentication that body text legitimately named it; an attacker can name an existing ID.

PR #2168 is still open and its anchoring changes are not on this branch, so I won’t assume that follow-up has landed. The prescribed `/go:discover-related` helper is not available in this session; I performed the equivalent manual search across definitions, every caller, tests, and history. I’m now switching from the read-only review into the scoped implementation.

## Review findings and recommendation

The issue is real, but final-block-only parsing everywhere is incompatible with supported squash-resume behavior. Legitimate GitHub and native Git squash messages place original checkpoint trailers in body paragraphs.

Recommendation: narrow and evolve the experiment.

- Whole-message parsing remains for historical discovery and squash resume.
- New final-trailer-block APIs guard checkpoint creation, mutation, and reuse.
- Commit hooks and attach now ignore checkpoint-shaped body text.
- Storage existence validates discovered resume candidates, but cannot authenticate them. Fully eliminating that ambiguity would require a new authenticated checkpoint-to-commit association or removing squash-body discovery.

PR [#2168](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2168) remains open, so its broader line-anchoring work was not assumed or duplicated.

- Added production-boundary regressions in [manual_commit_worktree_session_test.go](/Users/muskanpaliwal/Work/open-source/entire/cli/fix-checkpoint-trailer-block/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_worktree_session_test.go:54) and [attach_test.go](/Users/muskanpaliwal/Work/open-source/entire/cli/fix-checkpoint-trailer-block/cmd/entire/cli/attach_test.go:2021).
- Preserved the original real squash fixtures and historical parsing behavior.
